quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They believe other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
They expect no favors and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to handle them.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down; a curving road is ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: Drivers must follow orders from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers whose vehicles broke down on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must follow signals from flaggers. They help keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: When driving on a road with a single broken white center line:

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross the center line to change lanes.
You can only change lanes from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross the center line to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic moves in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Remove your foot from the gas pedal. Do not brake. Let the car slow down on its own. Use brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: You should signal while turning because it:

options.text: Is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This helps other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit based on conditions, but never faster. Reduce speed for curves, hills with limited sight, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt worse than concrete or asphalt. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without planning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without planning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Make sure no vehicles are in your path. Use your turn signal to let others know you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you:

options.text: Should drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Should wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
Should wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic on a street or highway, wait for a gap wide enough for your vehicle to reach the speed of other cars.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic. The only exception is if traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Passing cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: You must yield to oncoming cars that are going straight. Only turn left when it is safe and you won't affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual place, you should:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for making sure your parked car is not a hazard. Park where drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam lights.
Use your low beam lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights you can use with low beams.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because motorcycles are small and don't take up much space.
Honk to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.
Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. If you return to your lane too quickly, the rider may swerve and crash.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic merging in from the right.
Merge to the right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging in from the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic will merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a crash.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when it is necessary to prevent a crash. Do not use it to make slow drivers go faster or to get them out of your way.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your driving, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain or fog. Even if they don't help you see much, low beams make it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn is allowed here.
You can turn left only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn is allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass.
Everyone can pass.
Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When a solid line is next to a dashed line, only drivers next to the dashed line can pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: How should you use the gas pedal?

options.text: Slowly and smoothly.
As quickly as possible.
By tapping it lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Press the gas pedal slowly and smoothly. Pressing it too quickly can cause the wheels to spin or the car to slide, especially on wet roads.
